title: Kernel change eval drift notes - flash-v2 + paged-kv + cont-batching
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a focused evaluation pass against the new runtime kernels and scheduling changes landed in PR #892 (flash-attention v2 + paged KV rewrite + continuous batching scheduler). The goal: detect functional regressions (semantic quality), performance regressions (latency/cost), and workload-dependent variance (prompt-set sensitivity). This is an iterative working doc — notes, intermediate outputs, and hypotheses are intentionally included.

Summary (top-level):
- Flash-attention v2 reduces P50 token latency for long contexts but introduced subtle tokenization-sensitive truncation on a small set of instruction prompts (see Observations).
- Paged KV (16k page size) enables 2.6x effective context for the QA and summarization suites but increases tail latency for short requests when combined with cont-batching due to page activation overhead.
- Continuous batching change yields 18% lower average token cost under sustained load but increases P95 latency by ~12% for single-request bursts unless fallback fast-path is triggered.
- Net: throughput / cost wins across heavy workloads; single-request latency-sensitive apps will need policy adjustments or revert of scheduler for canary customers.

Experiment setup (replicable):
- Date range: 2025-02-05 -> 2025-02-25
- Baseline runtime: runtime@main-2025-01-18 (flash-attn v1, legacy KV cache, fixed batching)
- Candidate runtime: runtime@feature/kernel-892 (flash-attn v2, paged-kv-16k, cont-batching-v2)
- Hardware: Dedicated VM pool (A100s), mixed instance sizes used to mimic prod: 8x A100-80GB (primary), 2x A100-40GB (edge).
- Models: rwd-7b-instruct (fp16), rwd-13b (q4_0) for long-context tests.
- Prompt sets: (kept as named sets so they match tracking):
  - ps-summary-news-5k (long document summarization; avg input tokens 4.2k)
  - ps-sql-generation (instruction-following, medium length; avg 200 tokens)
  - ps-dialogue-assistant (chat sims, short-turn latency sensitive; avg 40 tokens)
  - ps-long-context-qa (synthetic doc+question pairs, 10k-30k contexts)
  - ps-hallucination-check (bench for factuality/regression; includes reference answers)
- Evaluation harness: eval-runner v0.9.3 (same binary across runs). Sampling seeds fixed. Tokenizer v2.4.1 for both runs.

Metrics collected:
- Semantic: ROUGE-L (summaries), exact-match & F1 (qa/sql), instruction-following pass rate (binary), hallucination delta (measured vs reference), human-rated fluency sample (10 per prompt set).
- Perf: token P50/P90/P95 latency, request P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec throughput, GPU utilization, memory high-water mark, cost-per-token (inferred from utilization).
- Regression signal: per-prompt delta (candidate - baseline) for each metric; we especially flag negative quality deltas > 1.5% absolute or latency increases > 10%.

Results snapshot (aggregated) — numeric diffs reported as Candidate vs Baseline (cand - base):
1) ps-summary-news-5k (model: rwd-7b-instruct, n=200)
- ROUGE-L: -0.9 (baseline 42.1 -> cand 41.2) 
- Human fluency score (1-5): -0.1 (3.9 -> 3.8)
- Token P50 latency: -18ms (fast)
- Token P95 latency: +60ms (slower)
- Observation: summaries slightly more extractive; candidate sometimes drops the last sentence for docs with trailing bullet lists (look at sample ids S-103, S-158).

2) ps-long-context-qa (model: rwd-13b q4_0, n=150)
- Exact Match: +2.4% (better retrieval due to larger effective context via paged KV)
- F1: +1.9%
- Request P95 latency: +210ms (candidate 1.72s -> base 1.51s)
- GPU mem hwm: +1.8GB during page activation spikes
- Observation: large context answers improved coverage; latency spike tied to page warm-up when a request references cold pages.

3) ps-dialogue-assistant (model: rwd-7b-instruct, n=500)
- Instruction pass rate: -2.8% (candidate underperforms; failure cases mainly around turn continuity)
- Token P50 latency: -22ms (candidate faster)
- Request P95 latency: +14% (candidate slower)
- Hallucination-check: +0.6% hallucination rate (small increase)
- Observation: Continuous batching seems to re-order token emission in micro situations where the KV page boundaries coincide with response prefixes, causing inconsistent completion starts.

4) ps-sql-generation (model: rwd-7b-instruct, n=300)
- Exact match to reference SQL: -1.2%
- Execution correctness (synthetic runner): -0.8%
- Token latency improvements for medium tokens: -10ms P50, P95: +45ms
- Observation: a handful of prompts produce slightly truncated SELECT clauses. Suspect tokenizer/runtime cut boundary interaction with flash-attn v2 when attention mask edge aligns with token boundary.

5) ps-hallucination-check (mixed models, n=250)
- Hallucination delta: +1.4% (candidate worse)
- Human sample severity: small/medium (mostly minor hallucinated facts in long contexts)

Micro-analysis and hypotheses: 
- Flash-attention v2 optimization introduced an attention mask packing path that assumes contiguous KV chunk alignment. When paged-kv introduces non-contiguous physical chunks and the tokenizer produces subword splits at page seams, some attention indices are misaligned by 1 token in the packed buffer leading to off-by-one context leakage or truncation on ~0.6% of prompts.
- Paged KV warm-up: first access to a page triggers synchronous copy + kernel TLB-style remap that is amortized across long sessions but costs ~180-260ms on cold requests.
- Continuous batching tradeoff: scheduler now favors throughput via batching windows; small-burst low-concurrency workloads don't hit the fast-path early-exit heuristic leading to slight P95 increases.

Repro samples (IDs & quick notes):
- S-103 (ps-summary-news-5k): last paragraph dropped in candidate; tokens show abrupt end at token idx 10245 in packed buffer.
- Q-027 (ps-long-context-qa): improved answer with page-scan but request had +300ms cold-page hit.
- D-412 (ps-dialogue-assistant): assistant repeats previous-turn end; audible misaligned attention on token boundary 37.
- SQL-88 (ps-sql-generation): missing ORDER BY clause in candidate output.

Quick sanity checks performed:
- Re-run candidate on single-CPU debug mode with flash-attn v2 disabled: regression disappears for S-103 and SQL-88.
- Re-run with paged-kv turned to legacy mode: long-context gains disappear but short-request P95 returns to baseline.
- Re-run continuous batching with aggressive fast-path threshold: P95 drops ~9% back toward baseline and instruction pass rate improves ~1.4%.

Risk classification and customer impact: 
- High (requires mitigation before wider rollout): dialogue-assistant and SQL generation customers that are latency-sensitive or rely on exact-text outputs.
- Medium: apps that rely on long-context QA benefit but need to tolerate increased tail latency for cold workloads.
- Low: batch-only inference customers (steady traffic) — will see cost/throughput improvements.

Proposed mitigation plan (short-term):
1) Gate rollout: keep feature branch enabled only for dedicated pools with warm-up hooks.
2) Quick fix: revert flash-attn packing heuristic for token boundaries crossing page seams (PR idea: add mask-correct path when KV page boundary detected). Target: PR by 2025-03-05.
3) Scheduler tweak: lower batching window on low-concurrency pools and enable fast-path trigger on single-request latency budgets.
4) Telemetry: add counters for page-warm events, page-cold latency, and misaligned-attention-detections; surface as Console dashboard.
5) Evals: add targeted regression checks to CI for the 4 failing prompt ids above and increase human-sample size for hallucination checks.

Action items (owners):
- Asha: draft PR for packing heuristic change (due 2025-03-05)
- Marcus: add page-warm telemetry and dashboard (due 2025-03-10)
- Lina: extend eval harness with the three failing sample checks + automate rerun on PRs (due 2025-03-07)
- Tomás: run extended perf runs with mixed hardware to estimate cost delta across cold/warm mixes (due 2025-03-12)

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is tokenizer v2.4.1 fully compatible with the paged-kv packing layout? Need closer look at tokenizer offsets across page boundaries.
- Should we expose per-request page prefetch API for customers to opt-in? Useful for long docs ingestion but adds complexity.
- Consider adding an internal microbench for page activation cost to feed the autoscaler.

Appendix (quick links & artifacts):
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/892 (kernel changes)
- Bench scripts: gitlab:ci/benchmarks/kernel-eval-2025 (private repo link)
- Failing sample snippets: confluence:applied-ml/regen-samples-892

Notes (informal):
- Meeting planned 2025-03-02 10:00 PT to decide rollout. Bring SRE + product owners from Dedicated.
- Some of the quality diffs are subtle; human double-blind eval for the summary set recommended before any revert.
- Keep this doc as working; will copy final decisions to Confluence once action items closed.
